b: Autodesk announced changes to their popular Fusion software, which is used by professionals as well as 3D printing and CNC hobbyists and small businesses.
The announcement starts off with “as Fusion evolves into an AI-First design and manufacturing platform…”
Instead of starting with the basic software and buying the modules you need, there will be 4 new plans.
Starter (Free) – Free for personal projects, Core CAD, basic CAM.
Standard ($680/year) – adds Core 3D CAD, Integrated CAM, PCB Design, “built for individual professionals.”
Professional ($1150/year) – adds Advanced Design, Simulation, Nesting, Advanced Manufacturing (e.g. 3+2 machining, turn milling), Data Management, Team Roles.
Enterprise ($2250/year) – adds Design Manufacturing, Multi-Axis Machining, Generative Design.
They say each will have AI workflows built-in, and AI capacity tiered to the subscription type.
“No separate extensions or bundles to manage.”
But, as they mention “generative design” in the enterprise version, there’s the implication that “AI capacity” really means “AI capabilities.”
Here’s how current subscriptions will be mapped over to the new Starter, Professional, and Enterprise editions.
Autodesk says that if you buy the Standard plan now, before January 28, 2027, you can get Professional capabilities for 2 years at the Standard plan pricing.
The response from individuals has been extremely negative, with the shocked and unhappy reactions on social media platforms being what clued me into the announcement.
Individual users have expressed great displeasure about the “price doubling” for the features they presently use.

Autodesk’s Fusion plan mapping does show that “Fusion” will convert to a “Fusion Professional” plan. I guess that’s why they’re advertising that subscribing before the change will lock in the Professional plan at Standard plan pricing for 2 years. That’s the current plan for the standard “Fusion” subscription.
It seems that if you commit to 2 more years, you get to spend the same amount that you’re paying now, and that the price will only change after that period is up.
As you can imagine, this has prompted a lot more chatter about SolidCraft, the AI vibe-coded alternative.
I want to hear more about Fusion’s plans for how they will evolve into an “AI-first design and manufacturing platform.”
